title: fix(i18n): ar spells the standalone participle جارٍ pack-wide, not two ways
body:
Fixes #6610

The `ar` pack wrote the standalone منقوص active participle of جرى two ways at
once: `جارٍ` on 92 values and `جاري` on 8. One word, two spellings, one code
point apart — U+064D (tanwīn kasr, the yāʾ dropped) against U+064A (the yāʾ
kept). Eight values converged; no key added or removed, no `en` value touched.

## ⛔ The 92:8 majority is NOT why the 8 moved

A distribution cannot rule orthography, and this participle's ending is
genuinely **not invariant across syntactic positions**. An اسم منقوص declines
three ways:

| position | form | why |
|---|---|---|
| indefinite, nominative or genitive | `جارٍ` | the yāʾ **drops**, the rāʾ takes tanwīn kasr |
| indefinite, **accusative** | `جاريًا` | the yāʾ is **kept**, tanwīn fatḥ |
| **definite** (ال) or **annexed** (مضاف) | `الجاري` / `الجارية` | the yāʾ is **kept** |

So "the 8 are correct in their own grammatical context" was a live reading and
had to be falsified rather than out-voted. Four measurements did it.

### 1. The pack already distinguishes the positions — correctly

Three `ar` values keep the yāʾ, and all three are in positions that require it:

| key | value | why the yāʾ is correct |
|---|---|---|
| `console.ai.connectionStalled` | `لا يزال العمل جاريًا…` | khabar of لا يزال — accusative, tanwīn fatḥ on a kept yāʾ |
| `empty.appNotAvailableDescription` | `…قد يكون النشر ما زال جارياً.` | khabar of ما زال — accusative (tanwīn written on the alef) |
| `marketplace.installedAdditiveNote` | `…لكن النواة الجارية تبقي التطبيق…` | attributive on a definite noun (النواة) — definite |

A pack that were simply yāʾ-blind could not have got these right. That is the
strongest available evidence that `جارٍ` elsewhere is a position-sensitive
choice rather than a house tic — and it is the fact that makes reading (2)
below a measurement rather than a preference.

### 2. Per value: none of the 8 was in such a position

Reported per value, not as a total. All eight are the participle **opening the
string** (token index 0), so nothing governs them into the accusative; none
carries ال; and in none is the participle the مضاف — the maṣdar after it is the
delayed subject (مبتدأ مؤخر) of a fronted indefinite predicate (خبر مقدم), which
is nominative and indefinite. The annexed reading would turn a status message
into a bare noun phrase with no predication, which is not what the `en` says.

| key | ar before | ar after | en | render site | frame | annexed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid.loading` | `جاري تحميل الشبكة…` | `جارٍ تحميل الشبكة…` | `Loading grid…` | `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:2535` | participle + indefinite maṣdar heading an iḍāfa | no |
| `grid.refreshing` | `جاري التحديث…` | `جارٍ التحديث…` | `Refreshing…` | `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:4295` | participle + definite noun | no |
| `chart.loading` | `جاري تحميل الرسم البياني…` | `جارٍ تحميل الرسم البياني…` | `Loading chart…` | no call site — see the dead-key note below | participle + indefinite maṣdar | no |
| `console.initializing` | `جاري تهيئة التطبيق…` | `جارٍ تهيئة التطبيق…` | `Initializing application…` | `app-shell/src/chrome/LoadingScreen.tsx:87` — the heading | participle + indefinite maṣdar | no |
| `console.loadingSteps.connecting` | `جاري الاتصال بمصدر البيانات` | `جارٍ الاتصال بمصدر البيانات` | `Connecting to data source` | `LoadingScreen.tsx:56` — boot-step list item 1 | participle + definite noun | no |
| `console.loadingSteps.loadingConfig` | `جاري تحميل الإعدادات` | `جارٍ تحميل الإعدادات` | `Loading configuration` | `LoadingScreen.tsx:57` — list item 2 | participle + indefinite maṣdar | no |
| `console.loadingSteps.preparingWorkspace` | `جاري تجهيز مساحة العمل` | `جارٍ تجهيز مساحة العمل` | `Preparing workspace` | `LoadingScreen.tsx:58` — list item 3 | participle + indefinite maṣdar | no |
| `console.actions.retrying` | `جاري إعادة المحاولة…` | `جارٍ إعادة المحاولة…` | `Retrying…` | `LoadingScreen.tsx:118` — the retry button | participle + indefinite maṣdar | no |

The card's same-screen claim is confirmed from the source: `LoadingScreen.tsx`
renders `console.initializing` as the heading over the three
`console.loadingSteps.*` as a list, with `console.actions.retrying` on the retry
button — four of the eight on one screen.

### 3. ⭐ The minimal pairs settle it

Both syntactic frames occurred on **both** sides of the split — and five of the
eight had a word-for-word twin already spelled `جارٍ`:

| one of the 8 | its twin among the 92 |
|---|---|
| `grid.refreshing` `جاري التحديث…` | `list.refreshing` **`جارٍ التحديث…`** — the same two words, one code point apart |
| `console.loadingSteps.connecting` `جاري الاتصال…` | `topbar.connection.connecting` `جارٍ الاتصال…` |
| `grid.loading` / `chart.loading` / `console.loadingSteps.loadingConfig` `جاري تحميل …` | `list.loading` `جارٍ تحميل السجلات…`, `detail.loadingAttachments` `جارٍ تحميل المرفقات…` |
| `console.loadingSteps.preparingWorkspace` `جاري تجهيز …` | `console.ai.preparingConversation` `جارٍ تجهيز محادثة جديدة` |
| `console.actions.retrying` `جاري إعادة …` | `approvalsInbox.resubmitting` `جارٍ إعادة الإرسال…` |

`grid.refreshing` against `list.refreshing` is an exact minimal pair: identical
apart from that one code point. Two spellings of one phrase cannot both be
contextually correct, so possibility 2 fails on this pair alone; the other four
make it a pattern rather than an accident.

### 4. The 92 needed nothing

Zero of the 92 follow an accusative governor (كان / ما زال / لا يزال / إن …).
That zero is a measurement rather than a silence: **the same detector flagged
all three of the yāʾ-keeping values in (1)** — `لا يزال` and `ما زال` on the two
accusatives, `لكن` on the definite — so it demonstrably fires when there is
something to find. 91 of the 92 open their string; the one exception
(`console.ai.connectionOffline`, `انقطع الاتصال — جارٍ إعادة الاتصال…`) follows
an em dash, i.e. it opens a new clause.

⇒ **The 8 were the errors.** Pack is now 100:0.

## ⭐ Should the 8 join #5972's gate? No — and the reason is structural

I read #5972 and its pin (`ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`) before answering, and
the answer was measured rather than argued. That gate *derives* its population
from `en`:

```
const derived = PACKS.en.filter(([, value]) => value === LOADING_GROUP_EN).map(([key]) => key);
expect(derived.length, 'the group emptied or changed size ...').toBe(10);
expect([...derived].sort()).toEqual([...LOADING_GROUP].sort());
```

None of the 8 has `Loading…` as its `en` value — they are `Loading grid…`,
`Refreshing…`, `Loading chart…`, `Initializing application…`, `Connecting to
data source`, `Loading configuration`, `Preparing workspace`, `Retrying…`
(measured, table above). So adding them to `LOADING_GROUP` would break the
derivation check that is **that gate's own anti-vacuity guard** — i.e. widening
#5972 requires weakening it. The orthography split is a property of one pack's
spelling, not of a group of shared `en` strings.

So this takes the move `de-quote-pairing-3876.test.ts` already made instead, and
which the #3878 file names as its own precedent: a per-key list becomes a
**pack-wide invariant**. New file `ar-participle-orthography-6610.test.ts`:

- **the pack-wide rule** — no standalone `جاري`, no `جارى` (alef maqsura for the
  yāʾ), no bare `جار` with the tanwīn dropped, anywhere in `ar`. A ninth value
  fails **by key name** with no one editing the file, which is the half that
  lasts; the eight-value edit alone would have left the ninth to be written
  tomorrow.
- **the controls, asserted before any zero** — the matcher is run over synthetic
  probes inside the test: it must catch all three retired spellings and a
  leading و, and must **not** fire on `التجارية`/`التجاري` (the substring trap an
  ASCII word-boundary regex walks into), on accusative `جاريًا`, or on definite
  `الجارية`. `skeleton()` is asserted to actually strip. Without this the empty
  offender list would prove nothing.
- **the eight converged values pinned by name**, plus the `grid.refreshing` ===
  `list.refreshing` minimal pair, so the evidence for the direction is pinned as
  evidence and goes red if either side drifts back.
- **the three legitimate yāʾ occurrences pinned with their grammar** — the more
  important half. It is what notices a later "normalise the ar pack" sweep
  flattening a correct distinction into a real grammatical error, which is
  strictly worse than the inconsistency this card removed.

`ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts` changes only in its `ar` note: its present-tense
"the other 8 are a wider normalization filed separately" is now false, so it
records what happened and why widening it was not available. **No assertion in
that file is touched, weakened or added to.**

## Gate verdicts — every one quoted from its own printed line

All on the final commit `161494d4` with a clean tree. Heavy work ran through
`scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, whose verdict certifies the whole `&&` chain;
exit codes were captured by redirect-then-capture, never after a pipe.

Union run: `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 62s (1m02s) · waited 268s (4m28s)`

| gate | its own verdict line | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `vitest run packages/i18n/` | `Test Files 58 passed (58)` / `Tests 927 passed (927)` | 0 |
| `@object-ui/i18n type-check` | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, no output | 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` | `OK (scanned 5519 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)` | 0 |
| `check:i18n-keys` | `Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2831 keys) …` | 0 |
| `check:i18n-drift` | `No en value changed in this range.` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` | `3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-no-major` | `No changeset declares a major bump.` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-fixed` | `All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-overwrite` | `No pre-existing changeset was modified or deleted.` | 0 |
| `check-lint-coverage` | `lint coverage: 46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors (0 total).` | 0 |
| `check-vi-mock-specifiers` | `OK (3890 tracked source file(s), 2187 test-named; …)` | 0 |
| `check-shell-escape-residue` | `OK (4/4 root(s) resolved … 0 occurrence(s) outside a fence)` | 0 |

`check:i18n-dead-keys` ran but self-declares `This is a REPORT, not a gate`, so
it is not counted as a gate result.

**`check:control-bytes` is quoted above and a hand scan backs it**, since this
diff is a file full of non-ASCII:
`grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` over all four changed files
returned exit 1 (no match).

**Not measured, and said so rather than skipped**: the two `typecheck` invocations
`exclude` nothing relevant — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists
`locales/ar.ts`, `ar-participle-orthography-6610.test.ts` **and**
`ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts` in the program (lines 111/115/419 of 642), so the
green really does cover the new file.

**Lint is a declared narrowing**, with all three pieces of evidence:
`eslint .` inside `packages/i18n`, the only package touched; population read
from **eslint's own selection** via `--format json` = **84 files, 0 errors, 34
pre-existing warnings**, with all three edited/new source files present at 0/0;
invariance for untouched files = `eslint.config.js` configures **no type-aware
linting** (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService` — grepped, zero
rows), so a change confined to `packages/i18n` cannot move the verdict on any
file it does not itself contain. The repo-wide farm is CI's run.

## Ablation — 3 legs, each predicted before it ran, from the committed tree

Run under the lock from a **committed** tree, with
`trap restore EXIT INT TERM` using absolute paths resolved from
`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Each mutation was proven **on disk** by counting
the injected text and the removed text at the anchor (not by a bare
`git diff --stat` — the fix itself is an equal-length substitution, so the file's
byte count never moved and a size check would have proven nothing). Each restore
was proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`, and the tree was verified clean at the end.

**No rebuild was needed and none could have masked a result**: the pin imports
`../locales/index` — a **relative source** import, not the package `exports`
field — and `packages/i18n` has no `vitest.config.*` of its own, so nothing
resolves through `dist/`. Leg A proves this empirically: it mutates only
`ar.ts`, nothing is built, and the test goes red.

- **Leg A** — revert `console.loadingSteps.connecting` to the yāʾ spelling.
  Predicted red naming the key; observed **RED**, the offender assertion firing
  with `1 value(s) still use a retired spelling` and the message that tells the
  author what to write, plus the converged-census pin naming
  `ar console.loadingSteps.connecting moved`.
- **Leg B** — "normalise" `console.ai.connectionStalled` (`جاريًا`, where the yāʾ
  is required) to `جارٍ`. Predicted **red on the yāʾ-is-correct pin only, with
  the pack-wide rule staying green**, because `جارٍ` is not an offending form and
  the sweep structurally cannot see this defect. Observed exactly that:
  `1 failed | 3 passed`, `ar console.ai.connectionStalled lost "جاريًا" — khabar
  of لا يزال …`. That asymmetry is the whole reason the protective pin exists,
  and it is now demonstrated rather than asserted.
- **Leg C** — break the matcher itself (`skeleton()` made a no-op). Predicted red
  in the controls block first; observed **RED** there
  (`expected 'جارٍ' to be 'جار'`) before the pack-wide rule. A matcher that stops
  matching fails its own controls instead of reporting a clean pack.

⚠️ **One unpredicted diagnostic, reported rather than smoothed.** On the first
Leg A the non-vacuity floor was `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100)` — today's exact
count — so reverting one value tripped it at 99 and the failure a reader saw was
`no جارٍ found at all` instead of the offender list that names the key. An
exact-today floor is a ratchet pretending to be a proof of life. Commit
`8636f62a` slackens it to 80 with the reasoning recorded in the file, and Leg A
was re-run: it now fails on the offender assertion, as it should.

## Fences

- Diff is **4 files**: `locales/ar.ts`, the new pin, the `ar` note in
  `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`, and the changeset.
- ⛔ **The other nine packs are untouched** — `en.ts` is not in the diff at all,
  and `check:i18n-drift` independently prints `No en value changed in this
  range.` The all-locales parity gate did **not** force anything: no key set and
  no placeholder shape moved, so nothing here reaches the other packs.
- ⛔ No key added or removed; every change is a value edit on an existing line.
- ⛔ Every moved value keeps its U+2026 — #3878's glyph invariant is untouched
  and still green.
- `skip-changeset` **not** applied: a changeset is genuinely owed here
  (`check-changeset-presence` says so), and in this repo that label is a phantom
  that nothing reads, so applying it would only mint a false status.

## Examined and deliberately NOT folded in

- **Gender agreement.** Nine values put the masculine participle before a
  feminine maṣdar (`إعادة`, `إضافة`, `تهيئة`, `الموافقة`, `المعالجة`); strict
  agreement would want `جارية`. The impersonal frozen `جارٍ` is standard MSA UI
  register, and — load-bearing — the pack applied it **uniformly on both sides
  of this split** (7 of the 92, 2 of the 8), so it was never a distinguishing
  factor here and it is not a same-screen inconsistency. Ruling it needs an
  Arabic desk, so it is recorded in the pin's header as explicitly out of the
  file's green, not swept.
- **`chart.loading` has no consumer.** Grepped for the dotted key, for the
  `strings.x` object-access form that hides `console.*` from key greps, and for
  dynamic `t(...)` template construction. It is already a standing
  `[needs-review]` row in `check:i18n-dead-keys`, whose only textual references
  are now this pin and `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`, and that report says every
  hit wants a sampled human check before deletion (objectui#4658). Filing a card
  would duplicate an existing tracked line, so it is noted next to its pin row
  instead, with what to delete if it is ever retired.
